sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h10 widened (notes/hooks.md, round 3), the user's option 3 after q02's Easy result (2026-10-10: "option 3"). Medium target, hard welcome (no Easy slot). q02 (copper only, four names) measured "In band — Easy tier", Low 1/5; q03 is a different question (two metals, five names, "mine or source"), not a rewording: it adds one member and two decoys of a second kind. No platform result yet.
- Dependency plan: as q02 for copper (Doc 2 L21/L77-82, L119, L203; Doc 4 L80, L84/L106/L119, L171, L197; Doc 6 L76, L21, L92/L120, L135), plus lithium: Doc 2 L119 (the Industry Group mines lithium too), Doc 6 L110-111 (both SDIC companies added), L152-153 (SDIC Lop Nur produces potassium sulfate fertilizers; SDIC Lithium produces lithium carbonate; they "source potassium and lithium, respectively"), L164/L168 (Tianhongji: electrode materials for lithium batteries; sources carbon materials).
- Universe: every addition of the three updates. "copper" in an addition's description: Doc 2 L119, Doc 4 L171 (Ashele), L197, Doc 6 L135. "lithium": Doc 2 L119, Doc 6 L152-153 (SDIC pair), L164/L168 (Tianhongji) (caller's grep of all seven texts, 2026-10-10; no lithium in Doc 4). Members: the Industry Group (copper and lithium, mines), Zijin Mining (copper, extraction), Baiyin Nonferrous and Xinjiang Baiyin (sourcing copper), SDIC Lithium (sources lithium). Excluded: Ashele (first placed before the window), SDIC Lop Nur (potassium), Tianhongji (carbon materials for lithium-battery electrodes), Xinjiang Zijin Zinc and Xinjiang Zijin Nonferrous (zinc), gold companies.
- Necessity: unchanged from q02, which the platform's Document check measured (Run 4: Docs 2, 4 and 6 each needed; closed-book wrong): Doc 2 -> the Industry Group's activity and November 25, 2024 addition; Doc 4 -> Zijin Mining's copper activity (stated recall risk, local probes on q02: gold only as a p 0.3 runner-up without Doc 4, forced gold p 0.4 without Doc 2); Doc 6 -> the Baiyin pair and SDIC Lithium (post-cutoff, no substitute). No new probes: the added member and decoys are all in Doc 6.
- Selected-lever checks: Match, then exclude: without the "first placed" condition Ashele joins (six names). Mentions it vs does it: Tianhongji's description mentions lithium batteries and SDIC Lop Nur is named beside lithium, but neither mines or sources it; taking either gives six names, both seven. Scatter the pieces: Doc 2 one member, Doc 4 one, Doc 6 three.
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Out-of-range period, Uses the wrong period or date): Ashele taken as first placed in January 2025 -> gold plus Xinjiang Habahe Ashele Copper (six names); measured on q02's Run 4 (2 of 5 low attempts). Mode 2 (Look-alike company, Picks the wrong entity or section): SDIC Xinjiang Luobupo Potash taken with its lithium subsidiary -> gold plus the parent (six names); "respectively" (Doc 6 L153) assigns potassium to the parent. Considered and not declared (plausible, unmeasured): Tianhongji included for "lithium batteries"; Xinjiang Baiyin or the Industry Group omitted (q02 Run 4 had two incomplete low attempts).
- Calculation verification: not applicable (set).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no passage groups copper or lithium entities; the page overview gives names only. Searches for "copper" and "lithium" return the five members, Ashele, SDIC Lop Nur and Tianhongji; the shortest valid route checks each candidate's first placement and what its description says it mines or sources.
- Precision/readings: "first placed on the UFLPA Entity List" is the consolidated register; "from November 25, 2024 through August 3, 2026" includes both end updates. "mine or source": the Industry Group "mines ... copper, lithium"; Zijin's "exploration and extraction of metals, including ... copper" is mining; the Baiyin pair "are sourcing copper"; SDIC Lithium sources lithium from brine. "process" is left out on purpose so that a maker of battery materials is not arguable. The alias "Xinjiang Nonferrous" removed from East Hope (Doc 2 L163) is not said to be the Industry Group. Names are given without "Co., Ltd." so the list separators stay unambiguous.
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (notes/intake.json).
- Style/set review: 28 words, no em-dash. q02 (dropped after its Easy result) is this question's narrower predecessor; they are never both live. Five-item list without a stated count (List contract advisory), kept on purpose: a stated count would tell a solver holding six or seven candidates how many to drop.
- Warnings answered: pending the floor.

sections.question: In any order, which entities, if any, first placed on the UFLPA Entity List from November 25, 2024 through August 3, 2026 mine or source copper or lithium?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 2, summary, appendix 1 and the company's description): the update that publishes the UFLPA Entity List as of November 25, 2024 adds five entities to the section 2(d)(2)(B)(ii) list, one of them Xinjiang Nonferrous Metals Industry Group Co., Ltd., which "mines, smelts, and processes raw metallic materials, including copper, lithium". It was first placed on the list on November 25, 2024 and qualifies.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 2, the section 2(d)(2)(B)(ii) list as of November 25, 2024): Xinjiang Habahe Ashele Copper Co., Ltd. is already on that list but is not one of the update's five additions, so it was first placed on the list before November 25, 2024.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 4, appendix 1): the update that publishes the list as of January 15, 2025, superseding the November 25, 2024 list, adds thirty-five entities to the section 2(d)(2)(B)(v) list, among them Zijin Mining Group Co., Ltd. and Xinjiang Habahe Ashele Copper Co., Ltd.

Step 4. Source input (Doc 4, descriptions): Zijin Mining Group is "principally engaged in the exploration and extraction of metals, including zinc, copper", and it is on no earlier list, so it was first placed on January 15, 2025 and qualifies. Ashele mines copper, but its January 15, 2025 placement put an entity already on the list onto a second sub-list, so it is excluded. Xinjiang Zijin Zinc Industry Co., Ltd. and Xinjiang Zijin Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd. handle zinc only and do not qualify.

Step 5. Source input (Doc 6, appendix 1 and the Baiyin paragraph): the update that publishes the list as of August 3, 2026, superseding the January 15, 2025 list, adds forty-three new entities. Among them are Baiyin Nonferrous Group Co., Ltd. and its wholly-owned subsidiary Xinjiang Baiyin Mining Development Co., Ltd., and "Baiyin Nonferrous and Xinjiang Baiyin are sourcing copper and molybdenum from the XUAR", so both qualify.

Step 6. Source input (Doc 6, the SDIC paragraph): the same update adds SDIC Xinjiang Luobupo Potash Co., Ltd. and its wholly-owned subsidiary SDIC Xinjiang Lithium Industry Co., Ltd., which "source potassium and lithium, respectively". The subsidiary sources lithium and qualifies; the parent sources potassium and does not.

Step 7. Source input (Doc 6, the Xinjiang Tianhongji paragraph): Xinjiang Tianhongji Technology Co., Ltd. "produces negative electrode materials for lithium batteries" but "sources carbon materials", so it neither mines nor sources lithium and does not qualify.

Step 8. Completeness (Doc 2, Doc 4 and Doc 6): no other description of an entity these three updates add mentions copper or lithium; the Western Gold and Shandong Gold companies produce gold.

Step 9. Answer (Doc 2, Doc 4 and Doc 6): Xinjiang Nonferrous Metals Industry Group, Zijin Mining Group, Baiyin Nonferrous Group, Xinjiang Baiyin Mining Development and SDIC Xinjiang Lithium Industry, in any order.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Out-of-range period
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Look-alike company
How a careless solver fails: Picks the wrong entity or section

Why these are traps: Out-of-range period: Doc 4 adds Ashele Copper in January 2025, but Doc 2's November 25, 2024 list already carries it outside that update's five additions; including it gives six names. Look-alike company: Doc 6's SDIC Lop Nur Potash sources potassium; only subsidiary SDIC Lithium sources lithium; the parent fails.
